subject: OrchidBank: deployment segmentation, egress proofs, and fallback SLA
messages:
From: Anna Castillo <anna.castillo@orchidbank.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: OrchidBank Security Team <security@orchidbank.com>
Date: 2028-05-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: technical evidence for deployment segmentation and egress controls

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we move toward the procurement stage, our security team needs a concise packet addressing deployment segmentation and egress assurance for Redwood Inference when deployed in our VPC/dedicated environment. Specifically we need: 

- A network diagram showing tenant boundaries, sidecar proxies, and any public egress points.
- Concrete evidence of egress controls (flow logs, firewall rules, or attestations) we can use for our audit.
- A short threat-model summary covering lateral movement and exfiltration scenarios and corresponding mitigations.
- Confirmation of fallback behavior and any SLA adjustments if a primary zone degrades (we need failover timelines and scope of functionality during fallback).

Preferred format: PDF packet + supporting artifacts (logs or screenshots). Can you provide this by end of next week (target June 1)? Also note we may need an engineer-to-engineer call to review the diagrams.

Appreciate it — we want this in our submission to procurement next Friday.

Best,
Anna
Anna Castillo
Sr. Security Engineer, OrchidBank

[OrchidBank request: list of internal auditors attached as separate mail]

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Anna Castillo <anna.castillo@orchidbank.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-28T18:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: technical evidence for deployment segmentation and egress controls

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to assemble a focused packet. Quick confirmations:

- We'll provide a PDF packet that includes a high-resolution network diagram, a summarized threat model, and an SLA/fallback matrix.
- For "evidence" we can provide sanitized flow-log excerpts, firewall rule exports, and signed attestations from our infra team.
- Proposed delivery: by EOD 2028-06-01 (we can accelerate if you need a subset sooner).

Cc'ing Marcus (Infra lead) and Vanessa (Security & Compliance) to pull the artifacts and draft the threat summary. Marcus/Vanessa — can you assemble the attachments listed below and add any required screenshots/exports? I'd like a 1-page executive summary plus embedded appendix artifacts.

Next steps: once we send the packet I'll propose a 30-minute technical review session (you can pick times on the link below).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

[Meeting link: https://meet.redwood.com/neha/orchidbank-30m]

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-29T10:06:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: artifacts for OrchidBank packet

Neha / Vanessa — initial push: I pulled the references and sketched diagrams. Items I'm including: 

- network-segmentation-diagram.pdf (shows control plane, inference zones, sidecar layer, tenant KV boundaries, management plane access)
- inference-zone-mapping.png (per-region zone mapping with egress guards called out)
- egress-control-evidence.zip (contains sanitized VPC flow log snippets, security group exports, and bastion audit lines)

Technical notes for the threat-model summary (short bullets to include):
- Attack surface: sidecar to GPU host channels (mitigated by mutual TLS, per-tenant mTLS certs, and non-privileged containers)
- KV cache confidentiality: KV cache resides in per-tenant process memory with strict kernel namespaces; no cross-tenant sharding permitted
- Egress: outbound allowed only via vetted egress proxies with signed attestations; everything else drop
- Failover: cold fallback to regional read-only variants (model-serving continues with reduced throughput); KV-cache warmup strategy and client-backoff guidance included

I'll attach the artifacts to the packet and feed to Vanessa for compliance language.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference

[Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/secure/ORB-47/segmentation-packet]

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-31T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: artifacts for OrchidBank packet

Thanks — I've drafted the threat-model summary and added explicit mitigation references (SOC/controls mapping) for procurement review. Highlights to include in the executive summary: 

- Lateral movement mitigations: strict RBAC, process-level isolation, container seccomp profiles, host intrusion detection triggers (tripwire events forwarded to SIEM).
- Exfiltration mitigations: egress proxy enforced with allowlist, per-tenant egress token rotation, stream sampling for high-entropy data patterns, and DLP hooks at proxy tier.
- Evidence package: redacted flow logs + rule exports + timestamped bastion session records.
- SLA/fallback matrix: primary zone RPO=30s for control-plane failover; model-serving fallback to regional read-only with 85% throughput; full recovery target 12 hours for stateful caches (KV warmup dependent).

I've attached: threat-model-summary.docx and fallback-sla-matrix.xlsx (contains the RPO/RTO by component and customer-impact table).

Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Security Architect, Redwood Inference

[attachment: threat-model-summary.docx]

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Anna Castillo <anna.castillo@orchidbank.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: technical evidence for deployment segmentation and egress controls — packet attached

Hi Anna — attaching the packet we discussed. Summary below with pointers to the artifacts included.

--- Executive summary (1 paragraph):
Redwood Inference can run in your VPC with strict per-tenant isolation. The delivery packet includes network diagrams showing per-tenant inference zones, an evidence bundle with redacted flow logs and firewall rule exports, a concise threat-model summary aligned to your audit requirements, and a fallback/SLA matrix describing functional degradation and timelines during zone failover.

--- What we've attached (files):
- network-segmentation-diagram.pdf — high-resolution diagram of control plane, inference zones, sidecar proxies, and management access.
- inference-zone-mapping.png — region-by-region zone mapping, annotated with egress guard locations.
- egress-control-evidence.zip — sanitized VPC flow logs, SG/NACL exports, and bastion session timestamps.
- threat-model-summary.docx — 2-page summary mapping mitigations to potential attack paths.
- fallback-sla-matrix.xlsx — RPO/RTO table and customer-impact tiers.

--- Quick answers to your original asks: 
1) Network diagram: included (network-segmentation-diagram.pdf).
2) Evidence of egress controls: see egress-control-evidence.zip (we include pre-redaction snippets and audit timestamps; full raw logs can be shared under an NDA if required).
3) Threat model summary: see threat-model-summary.docx (covers lateral movement, KV cache confidentiality, and exfiltration mitigations).
4) Fallback behavior & SLA: fallback-sla-matrix.xlsx — primary zone failover behavior and expected functional scope during fallback are documented.

Quoted from your original: "Can you provide this by end of next week (target June 1)?" — Delivered. If you'd like, we can do a 30-minute walk-through where Marcus can show the diagram and Vanessa can run through the threat-model highlights. Use this link to pick a slot: https://meet.redwood.com/neha/orchidbank-30m

Let me know if you need anything else or want the raw evidence under NDA.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
